Source: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System) - MODIS C6.1
Site_Names: National grid coverage; not pre-filtered to landfill sites
Temporal_Resolution: Daily / Satellite overpasses (Terra morning ~10:30, Aqua afternoon ~13:30)
Gas_Measurements: None (No methane or hazardous gas fields)
Fire_Event_Labels: Satellite thermal anomalies (brightness temp 4um/11um, Fire Radiative Power in MW, confidence 0-100%, type: 0=presumed vegetation, 2=static land source)
Temperature_Measurements: Brightness temp (Kelvin): brightness (channel 21/22, ~4 um) and bright_t31 (channel 31, ~11 um)
Quality_Concerns: MODIS detects all thermal anomalies (agricultural burning, forest fires, industrial heat). Landfill fires are unlabelled within the general fire population; spatial buffer intersection with known landfill boundaries is mandatory.
Verdict: B — Supporting dataset (Crucial for historical thermal anomaly screening over Indian landfills in 2025; cannot predict future fires alone)
Compatibility_Notes: Pairs directly with Ghazipur, Bhalswa, Deonar, Brahmapuram coordinates via spatial buffer (1-2 km); pairs temporally with ERA5 weather reanalysis.

Source: Published scientific study on North American Elevated Temperature Landfills (Ohio EPA / SciHub repository)
Sheets: 15 sheets (Fig 1, 2A-3A, 2B-3B, 2C-3C, 2D-3D, 2E-3E, 4A, 4B, 5A, 5B, 6, S1, S2, S3, Data dictionary)
Geographic_Coverage: United States (5 distinct landfills: ETLF A, B, C, D, E; includes Ohio sites)
Site_Names: ETLF A (Countywide MSW/industrial), ETLF B, ETLF C, ETLF D, ETLF E
Coordinates_Available: Facility-level ID only (no exact lat/lon in sheets to protect commercial identity)
Gas_Measurements: CH4 (%), CO2 (%), O2 (%), CO (ppmv), H2 (%), N2 (%), CH4/CO2 ratio
Fire_Event_Labels: Subsurface Exothermic Reaction / Elevated Temperature alert levels (Low Alert, Low Caution, Good, High Caution, High Alert)
Temperature_Measurements: Internal landfill wellhead gas temperature (°C) ranging from ambient to 85°C+
Missing_Data_Issues: Clean published research data; minor nulls in supplementary notes
Quality_Concerns: Internal wellhead measurements, NOT surface or satellite emissions. Facility coordinates masked to letter IDs (A–E).
Measurement_Type: Direct in-situ landfill gas extraction wellhead measurements
Verdict: A — Core candidate (Gold-standard ground-truth dataset for internal thermal-gas relationships, subsurface heating, and smouldering risk classification)
Inspection_Status: Fully inspected (15 sheets parsed via Excel COM, schema and row counts verified)
Compatibility_Notes: Directly supports classification of subsurface elevated-temperature risk; pairs with Bridgeton (k6) for cross-site validation.

Source: Missouri Department of Natural Resources (MDNR) / Bridgeton Landfill Subsurface Smoldering Fire Investigation (Companion to Paper k6)
Geographic_Coverage: Bridgeton Landfill, Missouri, United States (38.7618° N, 90.4347° W)
Site_Names: Bridgeton Landfill (individual gas extraction wells: GEW-01 to GEW-100+)
Temporal_Resolution: Daily to bi-weekly individual well measurements
Coordinates_Available: Landfill coordinates known; well IDs explicitly tracked
Gas_Measurements: CH4 (%), CO2 (%), O2 (%), Residual N2 (%), Ratio CH4/CO2
Fire_Event_Labels: Risk_Category (Low, Medium, High Risk of Subsurface Elevated Temperature / Smouldering reaction)
Temperature_Measurements: Internal wellhead temperature in Fahrenheit (°F) and Celsius (°C)
Weather_Variables: None directly embedded (can be paired with NOAA / ERA5 for St. Louis)
Quality_Concerns: Single site experiencing active subsurface smouldering reaction; non-reaction wells serve as local controls.
Measurement_Type: Regulatory and operational in-situ gas wellhead monitoring
Verdict: A — Core candidate (Essential ground-truth dataset for training and evaluating supervised subsurface fire-risk classification models)
Inspection_Status: Fully inspected (18,469 rows verified, all 10 columns audited)
Compatibility_Notes: Directly compatible with RSET risk index and ETLF Gas SciHub; can be trained with Random Forest / XGBoost to predict fire risk categories.

Source: GHGSat high-resolution satellite commercial constellation (151 waste sites study)
Geographic_Coverage: Global (151 waste disposal sites across North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa)
Temporal_Resolution: Targeted satellite overpass snapshots (~25 m spatial resolution)
Coordinates_Available: Yes (lat, lon of plume centroid and manually pinned sources)
Gas_Measurements: Methane emission rate Q_t_per_hr (tonnes/h), Q_error_t_per_hr, Integrated Methane Enhancement IME_kg, conversion factor
Missing_Data_Issues: 0% nulls in key emission and coordinate fields
Quality_Concerns: Intermittent targeted snapshots (clear-sky only); detection threshold ~100–200 kg/h; zero plumes not explicitly recorded in this file (only detections).
Measurement_Type: Satellite point-source hyperspectral / Fabry-Perot interferometer retrieval
Verdict: A — Core candidate (Primary high-resolution satellite methane plume dataset for hotspot detection and emission quantification)
Compatibility_Notes: Pairs with GHGSat_landfill_survey_Dataset.xlsx for facility-level model comparison; pairs with ERA5 for wind validation.

Source: Nature / ES&T publication supplementary dataset (Sixty North American Landfills survey)
Sheets: 6 data sheets (Figure 1, Data Dictionary, Figure 2, Figure 3, Figures 4 and 5, Figure 6, Figure 7)
Geographic_Coverage: North America (United States and Canada, 60 municipal solid waste landfills)
Temporal_Resolution: Overpass dates and model comparison annual/monthly
Coordinates_Available: Site IDs mapped in GIS (ArcGIS map data in Fig 2)
Gas_Measurements: GHGSat (kg CH4/h), FOD Model (kg CH4/h), CEA Model (kg CH4/h), Methane Collected (kg CH4/h), Carbon Mapper (kg CH4/h)
Quality_Concerns: Demonstrates substantial discrepancies between satellite-measured emissions and regulatory inventory models (FOD/EPA).
Measurement_Type: Multi-source synthesis (Satellite observations + regulatory model estimates + facility gas capture records)
Verdict: B — Supporting dataset (Vital for benchmarking multi-source consistency and demonstrating model vs measurement gaps)
Compatibility_Notes: Directly matches GHGSat_detected_plumes.csv and Carbon Mapper observations for North American sites.

Source: Carbon Mapper airborne remote sensing campaigns (AVIRIS-NG / GAO spectrometers)
Geographic_Coverage: United States (California, Texas, Southwest, East Coast airborne transects)
Temporal_Resolution: Flight line survey snapshots (~5 m spatial resolution)
Gas_Measurements: Instantaneous methane emission rate qplume (kg/h), uncertainty sigma_qplume (kg/h)
Missing_Data_Issues: 0% nulls in plume coordinates and emission rates
Quality_Concerns: High spatial resolution (5 m) but airborne campaign-based; sporadic coverage restricted to flyover dates.
Verdict: B — Supporting dataset (Excellent fine-scale spatial validation for satellite methane plumes and hotspot boundary delineation)
Compatibility_Notes: Directly compatible with Landfill_plume_detections.csv and GHGSat surveys over California and US landfills.

Source: Carbon Mapper / US EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) facility linkage
Site_Names: GHGRP ID (7-digit EPA facility identifier, e.g., 1005717)
Temporal_Resolution: Airborne detection timestamps (embedded in candidate ID)
Coordinates_Available: Yes (Latitude of Plume Origin, Longitude of Plume Origin)
Missing_Data_Issues: Contains 451 duplicate rows from concatenated flight reports; deduplication required before training.
Quality_Concerns: Includes facility ID linkage to EPA databases; duplicate candidate IDs present.
Measurement_Type: Airborne remote sensing mapped to facility inventories
Verdict: B — Supporting dataset (Direct bridge connecting Carbon Mapper plumes to US EPA LMOP facility metadata)
Inspection_Status: Fully inspected (1,714 rows audited, 451 duplicate rows flagged)
Compatibility_Notes: Links directly to landfilllmopdata.xlsx via GHGRP ID for landfill waste-in-place, gas collection, and depth.

Source: US EPA Landfill Methane Outreach Program (LMOP) Database (March 2024 edition)
Site_Names: 2,641 unique MSW landfill facilities (Landfill Name, State, County, Physical Address)
Time_Period: Historical to 2024 (Open years 1900–2024, Closure years through 2100+)
Coordinates_Available: Yes (Latitude, Longitude: 100% complete for all facilities)
Gas_Measurements: Modeled methane generation (mmscfd), LFG collected (mmscfd), flared, or utilized for energy projects
Weather_Variables: None embedded (state and county level location enables weather linkage)
Missing_Data_Issues: Some operational parameters optional for closed sites
Quality_Concerns: Static facility infrastructure database, not a time-series sensor feed.
Measurement_Type: Authoritative national environmental registry and engineering survey
Verdict: B — Supporting dataset (Provides facility ground-truth metadata: landfill area, depth, waste in place, liner type, gas collection status)
Compatibility_Notes: Primary join key (GHGRP ID / Landfill Name / Coordinates) for US satellite plumes (GHGSat, Carbon Mapper).

Source: Global Hyperspectral Landfill Super-Emitters Study (Nature / ES&T 2025 companion)
Geographic_Coverage: Global (33 countries/regions: India, Argentina, Turkey, Pakistan, Bangladesh, China, US, etc.)
Site_Names: 82 major global landfills (including Indian super-emitters: Ghazipur, Bhalswa, Deonar; Norte III, Odayeri)
Gas_Measurements: Quantified hyperspectral plume emissions (t/h), uncertainty (t/h), Climate TRACE emissions (t/yr), WasteMAP (t/yr)
Weather_Variables: Wind speed provided for flux inversion
Missing_Data_Issues: Empty values indicate no clear overpass or below detection threshold (explained in README)
Quality_Concerns: Focuses on super-emitters (>1–3 t/h detection threshold); small landfills omitted.
Measurement_Type: Multi-satellite hyperspectral retrieval (EMIT, EnMAP, PRISMA) + Global Inventories
Verdict: A — Core candidate (Provides verified global landfill coordinates, including major Indian sites, and quantified satellite emission baselines)
Inspection_Status: Fully inspected (all 5 sheets audited, README cross-checked)
Compatibility_Notes: Provides the essential geographic anchor linking Indian landfill coordinates to MODIS 2025 fire data.

Source: Hyperspectral satellite inversion summary repository (companion to landfills_hyper_obs)
Site_Names: Facility names across Argentina, Turkey, Pakistan, India, Spain, etc.
Gas_Measurements: Satellite emission rate (t/h), emission_uncertainty (%), plume_count, overpass count, Climate TRACE quantity and emission factor
Missing_Data_Issues: 0% nulls in coordinate and emission fields
Quality_Concerns: Summary statistics at facility level, not individual time-series transects.
Verdict: B — Supporting dataset (Summarizes multi-sensor satellite methane emission rates and detection frequency)
Compatibility_Notes: Pairs with landfills_hyper_obs.xlsx and NetCDF plume cases.

Source: Climate TRACE (Tracking Real-time Atmospheric Carbon Emissions) Solid Waste Database
Columns: Geopackage vector features (point geometries and attributes)
Geographic_Coverage: Global (Worldwide solid waste disposal sites across all countries, including India)
Coordinates_Available: Yes (WGS84 Point geometry: latitude, longitude for all 62,662 sites)
Gas_Measurements: Annual modeled methane emissions per site (tonnes CH4/yr)
Quality_Concerns: Model-derived activity estimates; spatial locations derived from satellite / open GIS mapping.
Verdict: B — Supporting dataset (Invaluable global GIS database of solid waste locations; enables spatial filtering of any satellite thermal anomaly dataset)
Compatibility_Notes: Can be directly queried in Python via sqlite3 or geopandas to intersect with MODIS 2025 fire points.

Source: Rajbandh Landfill research study, Khulna, Bangladesh (South Asian tropical landfill context)
Fire_Event_Labels: None directly labelled (LST thermal anomalies can be analyzed)
Temperature_Measurements: Land Surface Temperature LST_Celsius (Satellite-derived Landsat thermal infrared)
Weather_Variables: Specific_Humidity (kg/kg), Wind_Speed (m/s), Waste_tons, NDBI (Built-up index), NDVI (Vegetation index)
Quality_Concerns: Methane is modeled generation based on waste mass; LST and vegetation indices are satellite-observed.
Measurement_Type: Multi-source observational time-series (Landsat LST/NDVI + ERA5 weather + Waste records)
Verdict: A — Core candidate (Crucial South Asian regional dataset combining Land Surface Temperature (LST), meteorology, and waste tonnage over 24 years)
Inspection_Status: Fully inspected (289 months audited, all 10 columns verified)
Compatibility_Notes: Directly demonstrates multi-source data fusion between thermal remote sensing (LST), meteorological drivers, and landfill waste.

Source: Field research study at Bubanj Landfill, Niš, Serbia (Companion to Paper k5)
Geographic_Coverage: Bubanj Municipal Solid Waste Landfill, Niš, Serbia
Coordinates_Available: Landfill location known; well IDs tracked
Gas_Measurements: CH4 (% vol), CO2 (% vol), O2 (% vol), CO (ppm)
Fire_Event_Labels: CO indicator levels (CO > 50–100 ppm is standard indicator of subsurface smouldering)
Weather_Variables: Ambient temperature recorded alongside internal temperatures
Quality_Concerns: Small sample size (60 observations across 10 wells); represents a single measurement campaign.
Measurement_Type: Direct in-situ portable gas analyzer and thermocouple probe measurements
Verdict: B — Supporting dataset (Directly illustrates empirical coupling between ambient temperature, gas well temperature, CH4%, and CO ppm)
Compatibility_Notes: Supports physical validation of fire-gas indicators alongside ETLF and Bridgeton datasets.

Source: Fuzzy Fault Tree Analysis (FFTA) of Landfill Fire Incidents (Companion to Papers 1 & k4)
Geographic_Coverage: Landfill safety risk engineering (case study: Saravan / Iranian municipal landfills)
Site_Names: Municipal solid waste landfill risk assessment
Gas_Measurements: Methane accumulation basic events (BE4: Methane gas accumulation in waste layers, BE23: Reactive waste dumping)
Fire_Event_Labels: Top Event: Major landfill fire with difficult controlling (Failure Probability = 5.51%)
Temperature_Measurements: Thermal basic events (heat accumulation, spontaneous combustion)
Weather_Variables: Environmental factors (arid conditions, wind, solar radiation basic events)
Quality_Concerns: Expert-elicited fuzzy probabilities, NOT an empirical time-series sensor dataset.
Measurement_Type: Probabilistic safety assessment and Fault Tree model data
Verdict: C — Optional dataset (Useful for conceptual risk structuring and expert weighting; not suitable for statistical machine learning training)
Compatibility_Notes: Provides the causal hazard structure (Minimal Cut Sets) for conceptual framework design.

Source: Mobile Laboratory In-Situ Methane Transect Surveys across 5 New York Landfills (Cornell / NYSERDA study)
Sheets: 14 individual CSV files (High Acres, Mill Seat, Modern, Ontario, Seneca Meadows)
Geographic_Coverage: New York State, United States (5 large operating landfills)
Site_Names: High Acres, Mill Seat, Modern Landfill, Ontario County Landfill, Seneca Meadows Landfill
Coordinates_Available: Yes (Continuous GPS Latitude, Longitude: 100% complete along vehicle route)
Gas_Measurements: Ambient methane concentration CH4_ppm_qcls, CH4_ppb_qcls, CH4_ppm_picarro, CH4_ppm_scaled
Missing_Data_Issues: High data quality; instrument-specific calibration scaling provided
Quality_Concerns: Measures ambient downwind concentrations (ppm), NOT internal landfill temperatures or fire events.
Measurement_Type: Mobile laboratory cavity ring-down (Picarro) and quantum cascade laser spectrometer (QCLS) transects
Verdict: B — Supporting dataset (Exceptional empirical dataset for studying surface gas dispersion under micro-meteorological conditions)
Inspection_Status: Fully inspected (in-memory unzipped and audited across all 14 files, >312k rows)
Compatibility_Notes: Pairs directly with local meteorological sensors; illustrates high-frequency gas plume variability.

Source: ECMWF Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) - ERA5 Atmospheric Reanalysis
Columns: Multidimensional NetCDF grid (2952 valid_time steps x 2 lat x 2 lon)
Sheets: 2 NetCDF files: instant (t2m, u10, v10, d2m) and accum (total precipitation tp)
Time_Period: 2,952 hourly time steps (equivalent to 123 days of continuous hourly weather)
Temperature_Measurements: t2m (2-meter air temperature in Kelvin, can be converted to Celsius)
Weather_Variables: u10 (10m U-wind m/s), v10 (10m V-wind m/s), d2m (2m dewpoint temp K), tp (total precipitation m)
Quality_Concerns: Coarse spatial resolution (~25-31 km); represents atmospheric reanalysis rather than local landfill boundary layer.
Measurement_Type: Numerical weather prediction reanalysis model (data assimilation)
Verdict: B — Supporting dataset (Demonstrates ready-to-use hourly weather pipeline for temperature, wind, and precipitation fusion)
Inspection_Status: Fully inspected (NetCDF dimensions, variables, and metadata audited via netCDF4)
Compatibility_Notes: Pairs temporally with MODIS 2025 detections or satellite plume observations to extract wind and ambient temperature.

Source: Hyperspectral satellite plume retrievals (EnMAP, PRISMA, EMIT L3B products)
Columns: Variables: ch4 enhancement (ppb), u10, v10, sp, lat, lon
Sheets: NetCDF format files for individual landfill plume events
Site_Names: Kabd Landfill, Norte III Landfill, Tecnosilicatos Landfill
Temporal_Resolution: Instantaneous satellite overpasses (~30 m spatial resolution)
Coordinates_Available: Yes (Pixel-level latitude, longitude, and UTM projection grids)
Gas_Measurements: ch4 (methane column enhancement above background in ppb)
Weather_Variables: 10-meter wind components (u10, v10) and surface pressure (sp)
Quality_Concerns: High data complexity; requires spatial array processing.
Verdict: C — Optional dataset (Demonstrates spatial plume masking and visual hotspot structure; not required for tabular risk modeling)
Inspection_Status: Fully inspected (dimensions, variables, and coordinate grids verified)
Compatibility_Notes: Directly matches Plume_mask and S2_RGB satellite imagery folders.

Source: Landfill flux tower / eddy covariance measurement publication (Kim et al. ACP 2026 / EGUsphere)
Sheets: 3 flat CSV files (33 rows, 16 rows, 18 rows)
Temporal_Resolution: Binned monthly and meteorological response intervals
Gas_Measurements: Mean methane flux estimate (kg/h or mg/m2/day) with upper/lower bounds
Quality_Concerns: Aggregated regression summary data, not raw observation rows.
Measurement_Type: Micrometeorological eddy covariance flux tower synthesis
Verdict: C — Optional dataset (Provides empirical response curves showing how methane emissions rise with ambient temperature and fall with rising pressure)
Inspection_Status: Fully inspected (all 3 files parsed and audited)
Compatibility_Notes: Provides domain-expert physical priors for meteorological feature engineering.
